answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a thread as the anchor of the cost.
